Round 1, major: the triage load stops naming the backlog's source, so production shows no section while the page tests, which pass the prop by hand, stay green.
Round 1, major: the check matches only `Status` in its exact case, so `**status 2026-11-11: …**` shows as the title.
Rounds 3 and 4: leading symbols are not stripped before the check, so `~~Status …~~`, `_Status …_` or a zero-width space shows as the title.
Round 4, re-aimed at the mdast rewrite: an HTML tag is kept as plain text, so `<s>Status 2026-…</s>` shows as the title.

Answer (b): a status must stand in plain or bold text. With that check gone, `~~Status …~~` or a status in a code span is read as live instead of failing loudly.
Answer (b): the newest status by date wins across cells. Taking the last one found instead shows an older status from a later column.
Round 6, re-aimed: only the first status word in a cell is checked, so a second status in a prefix is dropped and a misspelled one accepted silently.
Rounds 6 to 8, re-aimed at the mdast rewrite (replacing 15-label-only-prefix-text-lost, whose code is gone): a code span's text counts as plain, so `` `Status 2026-…` `` is read as a live status.
Rounds 6 and 7, major: a backtick counts as paired whenever any later column holds one, so a lone backtick merges the columns between.
Round 7, major: a backslash-escaped backtick is read as a code delimiter, so columns merge.
Round 7, major: backtick runs pair by count of one, so a double-backtick span holding `|` is split.
Round 7, re-aimed: `**` inside a code span (`src/**`) is stripped from the sentence as if it were bold.
Round 7, re-aimed: the first sentence's search looks inside code spans, so a `. ` in code ends the sentence.
Round 7, re-aimed (replacing 21-single-emphasis-kept, now the library's job): text inside emphasis, strike or a link counts as plain, so `~~Status 2026-…~~` is read as a live status.
